summary: Interrogated the doc-contract preservation requirement (issue #112) against forge upgrade's deterministic vendoring contract (spec legacy-upgrade.md).
gaps: On a diverged doc contract, undefined whether upgrade overwrites, preserves-in-place, or merges — governs whether the client keeps edits and still receives harness updates.
Divergence-detection baseline undefined: client file vs the new shipped template, or vs the client's old vendored template.
Whether to write a per-contract backup file at all, given the client repo is git and upgrade requires a clean tree.
contradictions: Operator initially proposed an agent/LLM-driven merge inside forge upgrade, which contradicts the spec's deterministic, reproducible, git-diff-auditable vendoring contract (legacy-upgrade.md: one command, no residue) and would add a hard companion dependency.
resolutions: Deterministic fix only (operator-confirmed): the report names the replaced doc contracts, stops reporting their dirs as 'Untouched (project-owned)', and warns on divergence — no merge, no agent.

Divergence baseline = the client's current doc-contract file vs the NEW shipped template (operator-confirmed); with no backup file an unedited client whose contract the harness updated sees only an informative warning line.

NO backup file is written: forge upgrade requires a clean tree, so the client's prior content is already committed and git-recoverable; the warning points the operator at git diff. A .orig per contract would bloat the client repo every upgrade to re-store what git already holds. Project-specific content belongs in a project-owned sibling file (issue #112 workaround).
Agent-assisted reconciliation is OUT of scope for the deterministic core; a separate opt-in follow-up if wanted.

rounds.focus: scope given upgrade must stay deterministic
does per-upgrade backup bloat the client repo
rounds.outcome: drop .orig; git is the backup (clean-tree required); warn + point at git diff
